analysis.title: Coffee Break: A blue tsunami
key_insights: Democrats have won large majorities in the House and Senate in the US midterm elections, according to the report, giving Congress new checks on the executive branch that have been lacking over the last two years.
Democrats flipped control of some of the most staunchly Republican states. The report attributes this to voter discontent over cost-of-living issues.
Democratic control will be real but far from complete over President Trump's agenda.
Health care spending cuts are likely to face policy review, since health care was the leading issue in Democratic ad spending (AdImpact).
Opposition to data centres was a focus for both parties, which could bring legislation that slows AI spending.
Corruption was a prominent Democratic campaign theme, so investigations into contracts (e.g. blocking renewables projects and favouring fossil fuels) and quid pro quo deals are expected.
Congress has limited scope to address inflation because it lacks the tools to deal with two leading drivers: the war in Iran and tariffs.
The result weakens MAGA favourites such as JD Vance and Marco Rubio for the 2028 Republican nomination and might encourage a non-MAGA outsider to move toward the political centre.

Trump's reaction is the main unresolved question. Doubling down on unpopular policies would likely bring greater near-term market volatility and conflict with Republicans. Working with the new Congress could support markets into the 2028 elections.

sector_views.rationale: Health care was the leading issue in Democratic advertising, so policy reviews of health care spending cuts are expected. The report gives no explicit sector rating.
Opposition to data centres was a focus of both parties, which could bring legislation that slows AI spending. The report gives no explicit sector rating.
Democratic investigations are expected into contracts that blocked renewables projects and favoured fossil fuels. The report gives no explicit sector rating.

risk_factors: Trump doubles down on unpopular policies, exacerbating the damage and raising near-term market volatility.
Legislation that slows AI spending, following bipartisan opposition to data centres.
Conflict between Trump and a Republican party that may want to change course.
Congress lacks tools to address inflation drivers (the war in Iran and tariffs).
vol_and_positioning: If Trump doubles down on unpopular policies, the report expects an era of even greater market volatility in the near term.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democrats win House and Senate majorities
War in Iran cited as a leading driver of inflation and a source of voter discontent
US tariffs cited as a leading driver of inflation and a source of voter discontent
Trump says he is prepared to work with Democratic Congressional majorities while denying responsibility for the loss

key_data_points.metric: Democratic House seats won so far (218 needed for a majority)
key_data_points.context: Compared with 136 Republican seats, as of the 4 November 2026 count, which is still incomplete.
key_data_points.anchor: Democrats have won 225 of 435 seats in the House (with 218 needed for a majority)

key_data_points.metric: Democratic Senate seats won so far
key_data_points.context: Compared with 44 for Republicans, as of the 4 November 2026 count.
key_data_points.anchor: and 54 seats in the Senate compared to 44 for Republicans

key_data_points.metric: New York Times projected final Democratic House seats
key_data_points.anchor: Their current estimates call for a Democratic majority in the Senate of 55 seats to 45 and in the House of 258 to 177.

key_data_points.metric: New York Times projected final Democratic Senate seats
key_data_points.anchor: Their current estimates call for a Democratic majority in the Senate of 55 seats to 45

key_data_points.context: Immediately before the election. The projected results exceed this.
key_data_points.anchor: Cook Political Report (House 240 and Senate 53 Democrats) immediately before the election.

tension_points.bull_case: If Trump agrees to work with the new Congress, the new balance of power could support markets in the run-up to the 2028 elections. He has sounded conciliatory in interviews.
tension_points.bear_case: If Trump doubles down on unpopular policies, he is likely to exacerbate the damage, bringing greater near-term market volatility and conflict with a Republican party that will likely want to change course.

theme_stances.key_argument: Market direction depends on whether Trump doubles down on unpopular policies or works with the new Congress.
